This decrease in oil prices may have lifted investor sentiment, contributing to the market's positive move. Traders are watching Nvidia's stock recovery, as mentioned in the headlines from Yahoo Finance and StoneX.

The S&P 500 rose 1.53% to 7635.81, driven by Nvidia's stock recovery, while the Nasdaq surged 2.15% on CoreWeave's strong quarterly earnings results.

S&P 500 (+1.53% to 7635.81): Nvidia's Huang Affair Boosts Oil Prices. The S&P 500 rose 1.53% to 7635.81 as oil prices fell, likely due to the recent news about Nvidia's CEO, Jensen Huang, being accused of misconduct. This decrease in oil prices may have lifted investor sentiment, contributing to the market's positive move. Traders are watching Nvidia's stock recovery, as mentioned in the headlines from Yahoo Finance and StoneX.
Nasdaq (+2.15% to 25604.17): CoreWeave's Strong Results Boost Nasdaq. CoreWeave's strong quarterly earnings results have lifted the Nasdaq, with traders watching for signs of a tech rebound. The company's positive outlook has helped alleviate concerns about AI spending, which had been weighing on the market. This optimism has led to a surge in AI-related stocks, including CoreWeave.
10-Year Yield (+0.3% to 5.0): Treasury Yields Rise Amid Economic Uncertainty. Investors are watching for more economic data to gauge the impact of inflation on interest rates. The rise in Treasury yields suggests traders are concerned about inflation fears, as highlighted by Seeking Alpha [11]. This move is also being tracked by Japan's government bond yields, which jumped in response to the selloff in US Treasury bonds [10].
USD/JPY (+1.18% to 159.85): USD/JPY Rise: Yen Weakness. The USD/JPY pair rose as traders bet on a stronger US dollar due to expected interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve. This increased demand for the dollar led to a decline in the value of the Japanese yen, according to [15]. The WSJ and FXStreet reported on the same trend, with the WSJ stating that 'Yen Slumps as Fed Rate-Hike Bets Boost Dollar' [12].
Crude Oil (+0.86% to 86.78): Crude Oil Prices Rise. Crude oil prices rose 0.86% to 86.78, the strongest month since March, as traders watched Middle East supply risks persist [17]. The rebound was also driven by tensions at the Hormuz Strait, which has been a major concern for oil markets [18]. However, the move was not supported by the S&P 500 futures, which rose instead, indicating a mixed market sentiment [1].
Gold (-0.62% to 4005.1): Gold Falls on CPI Surprise. Gold prices fell 0.62% to 4005.1 as traders reacted to the release of the US Consumer Price Index (CPI) data, which showed a stronger-than-expected rise in inflation. This led to a lift in the US dollar and yields, making gold less attractive as a safe-haven asset [21]. The market is now watching how the Federal Reserve will respond to this data, and whether it will lead to tighter monetary policy [20].

- The Fed is considering a 50 bps rate hike, with officials divided on the pace of tightening monetary policy, according to The New York Times.

Industry desks:
- Agriculture: USDA Grain Report Sparks Market Focus. The recent USDA Grain Report has shifted market attention to corn, soybeans, and wheat prices [23, 24, 25]. As the report's new forecasts take center stage, traders are watching for any signs of changes in global demand and supply [23, 24, 25]. The mixed signals from US grain markets ahead of the USDA WASDE Report have investors on high alert for any potential price movements [24, 25].
- Mining: Copper Prices Boost Mining Sales. Higher copper prices are helping mining companies like Barrick to boost their sales, but gold production is struggling to regain momentum [28, 32]. The surge in copper prices is also causing supply chain issues, with data center demand straining supplies and leading to a 35% increase in copper prices [29]. Meanwhile, silver prices are also rising, with a 2.22% increase on November 09, and silver prices are up 10.2% from last week [30, 31].
- Timber: Log Costs Soar in Central Europe. Log costs are rising in Central Europe, causing sawmills to pay double for their logs, which is affecting the entire timber industry [34]. This increase in log costs is also leading to slower lumber demand, as manufacturers struggle to absorb the higher costs [35]. Despite this, some timber stocks are still seeing upside, as investors remain optimistic about the industry's recovery [36].
